headline: Computational inference integrates sparse spatial and single-cell measurements across…
label: Single Cell Spatial Multi Omics
summary: Unpaired, weakly anchored, and histology-derived inputs are now being integrated into tissue-level single-cell profiles.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference that extends sparse, unpaired, or partially anchored single-cell and spatial measurements into tissue-level profiles. Morpho-FM predicts spatial gene expression from routine H&E slides using a pretrained single-cell transcriptomic foundation-model prior, and CANVAS infers tumor cellular neighborhoods and habitats from H&E after training on 41-plex spatial proteomics of 18M cells. Trajectory inference on Xenium 5k data from six IPF lungs (>630,000 cells) reconstructs a pseudo-temporal axis of fibrotic epithelial states. Other items address measurement fidelity and analysis: DeLeakage corrects transcript leakage across spatial transcriptomics platforms, EMD-HVG selects highly variable genes without normalization, and PhenoBIC classifies multiplex imaging phenotypes without manual gating. What is new is the extension to histology-derived inputs and same-section metabolite and transcript imaging, as Stereo-meta-seq couples MALDI-MSI with Stereo-seq to reveal DHA-driven proximal tubule maturation.
